claim: Consider markets with \(k\ge2\) firms, strictly positive integer firm sizes, and common total market size \(N\), with firm labels ignored. Let \(H=\sum_i s_i^2\) be the Herfindahl–Hirschman index and \(\mathrm{HTI}=1/(2\sum_{i=1}^k i s_i-1)\) be the Hall–Tideman index after ranking firms from largest to smallest. For every \(N\le9\), the two indices induce the same weak concentration ordering on every fixed-\((k,N)\) profile set. At \(N=10\), weak-order agreement first fails only through a tie: \((1,4,5)\) and \((2,2,6)\) have equal Hall–Tideman index \(5/11\), while HHI ranks the latter as more concentrated. No opposite strict ranking occurs for \(N\le11\). At \(N=12\), strict reversal appears for the first time, and across all firm counts there is exactly one unordered reversing pair up to firm permutation: \((1,2,4,5)\) versus \((2,2,2,6)\). Their HHI values are \(23/72<1/3\), while their Hall–Tideman values are \(6/17>1/3\). Thus HHI ranks \((2,2,2,6)\) as more concentrated, while Hall–Tideman ranks \((1,2,4,5)\) as more concentrated. The cutoff is exhaustive because positivity forces \(2\le k\le N\), and all positive integer partitions through \(N=12\) are checked by two independent generators with exact arithmetic.
integrity: At fixed total, HHI ordering reduces to the integer squared-size sum, while Hall–Tideman ordering reduces oppositely to the integer rank-weighted size sum. Every positive-integer profile through total twelve is enumerated by two independent generators, and all pairwise comparisons use exact arithmetic.
scientific_limitations: The theorem compares positive-integer firm-size profiles only at common firm count and common total market size. The twelve-unit cutoff is a discrete-resolution boundary and not an absolute market-size or policy threshold. The original Hall–Tideman full article was not available in the checked open or authorized institutional routes, so no whole-document noncoverage claim is made for it.
title: Twelve market units are the sharp HHI–Hall–Tideman strict-reversal boundary
